title: Money Managers Brace for 'Extreme' El Niño Cycle to Disrupt Markets
text: Money Managers Brace for 'Extreme' El Niño Cycle to Disrupt Markets The prospect of the world's strongest-ever El Niño cycle has investment managers preparing for significant market disruption. The climate phenomenon is driving up food prices and prompting economic revisions, affecting stressed markets with high debt and rising interest rates. Firms are developing strategies to mitigate the impacts of the associated extreme weather events. The prospect of the world's strongest ever El Niño cycle has a growing number of money managers racing to prepare their portfolios for the disruption they say is coming. The climate phenomenon, associated with warming across the equatorial Pacific Ocean, is fanning crop-damaging droughts and floods, driving up food commodity prices and prompting economists to revise estimates for inflation and deficits. These impacts are now feeding into markets already stressed by high debt levels and rising borrowing costs, making the ability to navigate the disruptions a priority for investors.Asset managers hedge against El Niño disruptionsNo corner of global asset markets will be fully shielded from the current El Niño cycle, says Katie Self, a portfolio manager at Pictet Asset Management. The firm is looking for companies designing technologies that will help cope with the extreme weather patterns, such as smart-irrigation equipment providers and flood protection systems. Other managers, like Man Group and T. Rowe Price, are turning to custom-made models to protect their portfolios.The consensus is that while El Niño is a natural weather cycle, the interaction with a much warmer baseline climate will make the consequences substantially worse than previous events.
